subject: Org kickoff: namespacing, delegated service keys & phased invite cadence
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Kim Patterson <kim@pilothealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Org kickoff: namespacing, delegated service keys & phased invite cadence

Hi Kim,

Great to meet you on the call earlier — thanks for the time. Per our discussion, we want to land the initial tenant setup and make sure PilotHealth can start a small pilot next week with two projects (clinical-research, support-bot).

Key asks from our side to unblock provisioning:
- Confirm preferred project name prefixes (we suggested "pilot-clinical" and "pilot-support").
- A single technical point-of-contact who can accept service keys via secure channel.
- Any org-level constraints (IP allowlist, SSO requirement, or KMS restrictions).

Proposed plan (high level):
1) Day 0-1: Create tenant, seed admin user, generate two scoped service keys (project-scoped, time-limited).
2) Day 2-3: Send invites to pilot users in phased cadence (admins first, then devs).
3) Day 4: Verify API access and run quick smoke tests.

I'll attach a lightweight checklist and an example delegated-service-keys payload for your infra team. Can you confirm the POC and preferred project prefixes?

Thanks,
Chloe
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: pilothealth_onboard_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), delegated-service-keys-example.json (application/json)

From: Kim Patterson <kim@pilothealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@pilothealth.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 11:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Org kickoff: namespacing, delegated service keys & phased invite cadence

Hi Chloe,

Thanks — looks good. POC is me (kim@pilothealth.com) and I'll loop in our infra lead if we need KMS/HSM approvals. Project prefixes are fine with the suggested names. A couple of notes from Procurement:
- We need a short summary of the data flows for our security review (can you attach a one-pager?).
- For service keys we prefer project-scoped keys with 30-day TTL for the pilot.

Can you also add a line item for audit logs retention in the checklist? We need to be able to demonstrate request logs for 90 days.

Best,
Kim
Technical Program Manager
PilotHealth

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Kim Patterson <kim@pilothealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Org kickoff: namespacing, delegated service keys & phased invite cadence

Hi Kim — thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is a one-page data flow summary and I've updated the checklist to call out audit-log retention (90 days) and the service-key TTL recommendation of 30 days for pilot.

Operational clarifications for your infra lead:
- We will create two project scopes under the tenant: "pilot-clinical" and "pilot-support".
- Each project will receive a scoped service key; keys are limited to specific API scopes (generation, embeddings read) and optionally bound to IP ranges.
- Admin invites (tenant admins + security reviewer) will go out on Day 1; developer invites on Day 2 in a staggered cadence to avoid burst onboarding.

Next steps for us internally: Monica will coordinate the actual tenant creation and key generation. Ben will set up the initial smoke tests and share the test tokens (ephemeral) with your infra lead once keys are accepted. Jonas I'll need you to confirm the audit-log retention configuration and whether we can expose a filtered log view for Procurement.

Kim — is there a preferred time Wednesday morning for a 30-min joint handoff to run through the checklist?

Best,
Chloe

---
Attachments: pilothealth_onboard_checklist.xlsx (updated), pilothealth_dataflow_onepager.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Org kickoff: namespacing, delegated service keys & phased invite cadence

Looping internal ops in — I will provision the tenant and seed the following roles and resources: 
- tenant admin: chloe.martin@redwood.ai (will be granted Owner for initial setup)
- project owners: ben.carter@redwood.ai (pilot-clinical), jonas.weber@redwood.ai (pilot-support)
- service keys: generate two project-scoped keys with 30-day TTL, mark keys as "ephemeral/pilot" in metadata
- audit logs: set retention to 90 days and create a "procurement-view" filtered view (read-only)

Operational questions for Rishi: can we follow the delegated service key payload format attached? If so, I'll generate example keys and the JSON and send to Kim via our secure transfer link. Also propose we schedule the staggered invites: Day 1 at 09:00 PT (admins), Day 2 at 09:00 PT (devs).

I'll attach the exact key payload we plan to send.

Thanks,
Monica
Implementation Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: delegated-service-keys-example.json (application/json)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Org kickoff: namespacing, delegated service keys & phased invite cadence

Thanks — confirmed.
- Delegated payload format looks good; we will namespace resource IDs as "pilothealth:pilot-clinical" and "pilothealth:pilot-support".
- I will enable IP bind option but leave it off by default for the pilot — Kim can request a bind if they have static egress.
- Audit-view: provisioning done, link created (read-only). I'll add a short note in the checklist explaining how Procurement can export the filtered logs.

Monica — please proceed with tenant creation tomorrow morning. Chloe — if Kim confirms Wednesday 10am ET (7am PT), I'll join the handoff to walk through key acceptance and log export.

-Rishi
Head of Implementation
Redwood Inference
